subject: general
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Last night, a thick fog caused a massive accident ______ the Expressway.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** 'on'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When talking about accidents and other incidents in specific locations especially roads, highways, or expressways, the preposition '**on**' is generally used.
 
• When we mention routes and paths or speak about incidents occurring on streets, roads, or highways, we use '**on**'.
 
• The content of the sentence suggests that the accident took place on the surface of the Expressway.
 
• Thus '**on**' is the most suitable preposition to use in this case.

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 1'** i.e.** 'on'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• '**at**' (Option 2) is typically used to denote a specific point or place, such as an address or a location. It might be used when the expressway is not being viewed as a route but as a certain point of incident, which isn't the case here.
 
• '**over**' (Option 3) and '**above**' (Option 4) can be used when we are referring to something happening above a certain point. However, these prepositions do not fit in this context because the accident happened 'on' the expressway, not above it.
